rows.name: small Mario (standing, facing right)
rows.notes: Standing small Mario metasprite = 8 OAM entries in a 2-wide x 4-tall (16x32) grid, sprite pattern table 0 ($0000), sprite palette 4. Only the bottom two rows are actually drawn; the top two rows are the blank tile $FC that SMB always emits as stack padding for the small form. Proof: list_sprites with no filter, paused in World 1-1 first screen (game_mode $0770=1), returned one palette-4 cluster - OAM index 1 x40 y177 tile $FC; index 2 x48 y177 tile $FC; index 3 x40 y185 tile $FC; index 4 x48 y185 tile $FC; index 5 x40 y193 tile $3A; index 6 x48 y193 tile $37; index 7 x40 y201 tile $4F; index 8 x48 y201 tile $4F with flip_h true; no fail. Offsets below are from the visible 16x16 top-left (screen x=40, y=193 = nametable anchor). tile $FC at (+0,-16) no flip; tile $FC at (+8,-16) no flip; tile $FC at (+0,-8) no flip; tile $FC at (+8,-8) no flip; tile $3A (head left half) at (+0,+0) no flip; tile $37 (head right half) at (+8,+0) no flip; tile $4F (torso/legs left) at (+0,+8) no flip; tile $4F (torso/legs right) at (+8,+8) H-flipped. Tiles are drawn from the SPRITE pattern table (sprite_pattern_addr 0), so the CHR ids equal the OAM tile bytes $3A/$37/$4F. (Big Mario by contrast uses a real 8-entry 16x32 stack, recorded under 0x08-0x17 / 0x20-0x27.)
rows.why: OAM $3A/$37 over $4F/$4F(h) under four $FC fillers, palette 4, sprite table $0000; rendered from sprite CHR they are small Mario standing, as drawn at (40,193)

rows.name: small Mario sprite palette (red cap/shirt, orange skin, olive linework)
rows.notes: Sprite palette 4, the palette small Mario is painted with in World 1-1 (list_sprites returned palette 4 for all 8 of his OAM entries). Live values [34,22,39,24] = slot 0 $22 periwinkle, slot 1 $16 red, slot 2 $27 orange, slot 3 $18 olive. Slot 0 is transparent for sprites - nothing of Mario is drawn with it. WHAT EACH SLOT PAINTS: slot 1 = $16 red = the cap and the shirt/body (the big solid red areas); slot 2 = $27 orange = the face/skin; slot 3 = $18 olive = the dark linework - cap and face outline, hair, eye, and the shoes. PROOF (write_palette + screenshot + pixel samples): while paused, write_palette palette 4 slot 1 -> nes_color 44 ($2C cyan), step_frame 1, screenshot - Mario's cap and body turned cyan while his face stayed orange and the outline stayed olive/dark, i.e. only the slot-1 pixels changed; get_pixel_color(45,193) then read rgb 72,205,222 = $2C cyan, while (44,196) read $27 orange and (43,196) read $18 olive. clear_palette_overrides restored slot 1 to $16 red (screenshot shows red Mario again, toggling only slot 1; the other slots were never written, so their roles are read from the unchanged pixels and the tile bitmaps). Caveat: this palette is shared by any other sprite the game draws with palette 4.
rows.why: after slot 1 was written $2C, Mario's cap and body are cyan in this screenshot (rgb 72,205,222 in his box) and face/hair are unchanged; slot 1 cap/body, 2 skin, 3 linework/hair/shoes as claimed

rows.name: HUD layout
rows.notes:
Status bar of Super Mario Bros. (World): fixed at the top of nametable 0, tile rows 2-3 (y pixels 16-31). Rows 0-1 are blank tile $24 (CHR $124). All glyphs are background tiles from BG pattern table $1000, drawn with BG palette 2 (slot 1 = $30 white); tiles are named by nametable id (chr = id + $100).
LABELS Row 2 (tile_y=2): 'MARIO' cols 3-7 ($16 $0A $1B $12 $18 = M A R I O); 'WORLD' cols 18-22 ($20 $18 $1B $15 $0D = W O R L D); 'TIME' cols 25-28 ($1D $12 $16 $0E = T I M E).
VALUES Row 3 (tile_y=3): score = SIX digits at cols 3-8 (under MARIO); coin icon = col 11 (tile $2E / CHR $12E, BG palette 3 because its attribute block is 3, slots 1 $27 orange + 3 $0F black); multiply sign 'x' = col 12 (tile $29 / CHR $129); coin count = TWO digits at cols 13-14; world/level digits = cols 19-21, i.e. world digit, dash $28, level digit (World 1-1 displays $01 $28 $01); TIME = THREE digits at cols 26-28.
PROOF: read_nametable 0 (x0,y0) 32x4 gives exactly this, and screenshots on the title screen and in World 1-1 match. In World 1-1 the status bar read MARIO 000000, coin x00, WORLD 1-1, TIME 335/340/357; on the title screen it reads the same labels with score 000000, coin x00, WORLD 1-1, and the three TIME digit cells left blank ($24). The coin at col 11 is a BACKGROUND tile, not the OAM sprite near it: get_region object mode at (91,28) returned 31 connected pixels of background palette 3, box (89,24)-(93,30), CHR 0x12E, and get_pixel_color(90,28) read $27 orange; get_tile_at_pixel(90,28) returned tile_id 46 ($2E) chr_tile 302 ($12E), palette 3. Scroll is 0 over the HUD (get_tile_at_pixel scroll_x=0 at every HUD pixel), so the bar stays put while the playfield scrolls.
rows.why: against the screenshot: MARIO cols 3-7, WORLD cols 18-22 with W $20, TIME cols 25-28 on row 2; score cols 3-8, coin icon background $2E at col 11 (palette 3), x $29 col 12, coins 13-14, 1-1 cols 19-21, TIME 26-28 on row 3; all right
